data.narrative:
AlixLabs is a Series A-stage company in Chips & Semiconductors founded by Jonas Sundqvist, Dmitry Suyatin, and Amin Karimi, having raised €15M to date. The valuation universe comprises 11 same-sector peers: 3 public companies (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) and 8 private firms including SambaNova Systems, Cerebras, PsiQuantum, Etched, and Tenstorrent.

Standard triangulation methods prove constrained here. Peer-median analysis is not applicable due to insufficient narrow-set comparables; while 11 same-sector peers exist, filtering by stage and valuation tier yields fewer than 3 datapoints at each level, making sector-wide median unreliable as a proxy for early-stage frontier-chip companies. The heterogeneity within semiconductor subsectors—spanning chip architecture, application domain, and go-to-market maturity—argues against blending across the full peer set.

The data does not support a specific valuation range at this time. Meaningful triangulation would require either: (i) access to recent pricing from the identified private peer set (SambaNova, Cerebras, et al.) at comparable stages; or (ii) sufficient Series A peers within a narrower architectural or end-market segment. The €15M raised provides a floor but does not establish post-money valuation without disclosure of dilution. Key uncertainties include stage-specific pricing dynamics in frontier chip development and the absence of recent comparable financing terms within the Series A cohort.
